![](images/98/98b3193783f0ac19bcb78035b133ad8dbf956528dfb7474606cc586d3bfecc34.png)

The area of $ABCD$ is $90{\text{ in}}^{2}.$   What is the area of $△BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16\cdot 21\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{56}^{∘} \\  & =168\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{56}^{∘} \\  & =139.278… \\  & ≈139{\text{ in}}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of  $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =139-90 \\  & =49{\text{ in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $28\,\text{cm}^{2}.$ The enclosing triangle $ABD$ has area $40\,\text{cm}^{2}$. What is the area of $\triangle BCD$?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The dashed segment $BD$ completes the enclosing triangle $ABD$. Its area is the sum of the areas of the quadrilateral and the missing triangle:

$$
A_{ABD}=A_{ABCD}+A_{BCD}.
$$

Subtract the quadrilateral's area:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{BCD}&=A_{ABD}-A_{ABCD}\\
&=40-28\\
&=12\,\text{cm}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

![Concave quadrilateral ABCD with dashed segment BD](images/87/872338605084c225802cf1e5b7069938fb5d6f61b9cbe85312d28ecc2baf8852.png)

The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $32\,\text{cm}^{2}.$ The area of $\triangle BCD$, rounded to the **nearest integer**, is {{field-1}} $\text{cm}^{2}$.

A scientific calculator is required.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The known sides $AB=12\,\text{cm}$ and $AD=9\,\text{cm}$ meet at the included angle $112^\circ$. Use the sine-area formula for the enclosing triangle $ABD$, with the calculator in degree mode:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{ABD}&=\frac12\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot\sin\angle BAD\\
&=\frac12\cdot12\cdot9\cdot\sin112^\circ\\
&=54\sin112^\circ\\
&\approx50.067928\,\text{cm}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $BCD$ is the part of $ABD$ outside the quadrilateral. Subtract before rounding, keeping the calculator's full precision:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{BCD}&=A_{ABD}-A_{ABCD}\\
&=54\sin112^\circ-32\\
&\approx18.067928\,\text{cm}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Rounded to the nearest integer, its area is $18\,\text{cm}^{2}$.

The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $31\,\text{cm}^{2}.$ The angle at $A$ is a right angle. What is the area of $\triangle BCD$?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First find the area of the enclosing triangle $ABD$. Since $AB$ and $AD$ are perpendicular, they are its base and height:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{ABD}&=\frac12\cdot AB\cdot AD\\
&=\frac12\cdot8\cdot12\\
&=48\,\text{cm}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The enclosing triangle consists of the quadrilateral and the missing triangle $BCD$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{BCD}&=A_{ABD}-A_{ABCD}\\
&=48-31\\
&=17\,\text{cm}^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

A scientific calculator is required.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First calculate the area of the enclosing triangle $ABD$. Use the two given sides and their included angle, with the calculator in degree mode.

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{ABD}&=\frac12\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot\sin\angle BAD\\&=\frac12\cdot 16\cdot 18\cdot\sin57^\circ\\&\approx120.768562\,\text{in}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The enclosing triangle consists of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ and the missing triangle $BCD$. Subtract the quadrilateral area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{BCD}&=A_{ABD}-A_{ABCD}\\&=144\sin57^\circ-83\\&\approx37.768562\,\text{in}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Keep full precision until this subtraction is complete. Rounded to the nearest integer, the area is $38\,\text{in}^{2}$.

A scientific calculator is required.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First calculate the area of the enclosing triangle $BCA$. Use the two given sides and their included angle, with the calculator in degree mode.

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{BCA}&=\frac12\cdot BC\cdot BA\cdot\sin\angle CBA\\&=\frac12\cdot 4\cdot 6\cdot\sin75^\circ\\&\approx11.591110\,\text{cm}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The enclosing triangle consists of the quadrilateral $BCDA$ and the missing triangle $CDA$. Subtract the quadrilateral area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{CDA}&=A_{BCA}-A_{BCDA}\\&=12\sin75^\circ-8\\&\approx3.591110\,\text{cm}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Keep full precision until this subtraction is complete. Rounded to the nearest integer, the area is $4\,\text{cm}^{2}$.

The area of $ABCD$ is $300\, \text{cm}^2.$  What is the area of $\triangle ABC$ rounded to the nearest integer?

![](images/c0/c06ffb123bdd24c3f83419767b6d1578223b8093089b79f91aae8f1fc6121305.png)
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ACD.$ We get 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot DA\cdot DC\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡D \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(25)(32)\operatorname{sin}⁡{70}^{∘} \\  & =400\operatorname{sin}⁡{70}^{∘} \\  & =375.877... \\  & ≈376\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ and $\triangle ACD$ gives the area of $\triangle ABC.$ Therefore, 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABC} & ={A}_{ACD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =376-300 \\  & =76\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
